title: CloudFront — CDN & Edge
subtitle: Serve content from 450+ edge locations worldwide — cache, compress, protect, and deliver at the speed of light

content.text: Physics sets a hard limit on response time: data can travel no faster than the speed of light. Mumbai to New York is ~140ms at the speed of light; realistic internet latency adds another 50-100ms. If your server is in us-east-1 and a user is in Mumbai, every request has a 200-300ms baseline latency — before your application does anything. A CDN solves this by caching your content at edge locations near users: Mumbai user hits a Mumbai edge location, response in 5ms.

content.filename: Create a CloudFront distribution for S3 website

content.text: Cache behaviors — the power of CloudFront

content.code:
A CloudFront distribution can have multiple 'behaviors' based on URL path:

PATH PATTERN         TTL           BEHAVIOR
/static/*            31536000s     Long cache (1 year) — hashed filenames
/*.js                31536000s     JS bundles with content hash in name
/*.css               31536000s     CSS with content hash in name
/api/*               0s            Never cache (proxy to API server)
/index.html          0s            Never cache (always fresh)
/* (default)         86400s        Cache 1 day

WHY DIFFERENT TTLs:
  Static assets (app.abc123.js) — filename includes content hash
  If content changes, filename changes → automatic cache bust
  So you can safely cache forever

  HTML files — reference the JS/CSS files by name
  Must be fresh so users get the latest js/css filenames
  Cache for 0 seconds (or very short)

  API responses — dynamic, must never be cached (unless you explicitly
  want edge caching for specific endpoints like public pricing pages)

content.filename: Free HTTPS certificate via AWS Certificate Manager
content.code:
# ACM (Certificate Manager) provides free SSL/TLS certificates
# For CloudFront, the certificate MUST be in us-east-1 (global service)

# Request a certificate
aws acm request-certificate \
  --domain-name myapp.com \
  --subject-alternative-names www.myapp.com \
  --validation-method DNS \
  --region us-east-1  # required for CloudFront

# ACM returns a CNAME record to add to your DNS
# Once validated, the certificate auto-renews forever

# In CloudFront distribution config:
# ViewerCertificate:
#   AcmCertificateArn: arn:aws:acm:us-east-1:xxx:certificate/xxx
#   SslSupportMethod: sni-only
#   MinimumProtocolVersion: TLSv1.2_2021

# ViewerProtocolPolicy: redirect-to-https
# → All HTTP requests are 301 redirected to HTTPS automatically

content.text: Always use CloudFront in front of your S3 website, not S3 directly. S3 website hosting doesn't support HTTPS for custom domains (only HTTP). CloudFront + ACM gives you free HTTPS with modern TLS. It also protects your S3 bucket from direct access (use OAC — Origin Access Control — to restrict S3 to only CloudFront). This prevents people from accessing the S3 URL directly and bypassing CloudFront.

questions.question: You deploy a new version of your React app to S3. Users are still seeing the old version. What's the most likely cause?
options: S3 hasn't finished replicating the files to all regions
CloudFront is serving a cached version of the old files — run a cache invalidation
The React app needs to be rebuilt for CloudFront compatibility
CloudFront automatically refreshes every 24 hours — wait for next refresh
questions.explanation: CloudFront caches responses at edge locations for the TTL you configured. After deploying new files to S3, cached edges still serve the old version until their TTL expires. To force an immediate refresh, run a cache invalidation: 'aws cloudfront create-invalidation --distribution-id E... --paths /*'. A better long-term strategy: use content-hashed filenames (Vite does this by default — app.a1b2c3d4.js) so new files have new names, never conflicting with cached old files. Only index.html needs invalidating.

faq.a: CloudFront's pricing: $0.0085 per GB data transfer (first 10TB), $0.0075 per 10,000 HTTPS requests. For a typical small website serving 100GB/month, that's $0.85/month in transfer + ~$0.075 in requests = under $1/month. For most apps, CloudFront + S3 is cheaper than any other hosting option and faster for global users.

examples: Amazon Prime Video uses CloudFront to stream to 200+ countries. The 450+ edge locations mean your video starts buffering from a server within ~50km of you, regardless of where Amazon's origin servers are
CloudFront's AWS Shield Standard (free, included) protects all distributions from common DDoS attacks — absorbing up to Tbps of volumetric traffic at the edge before it reaches your origin
